Analog Atlas

How it works

The workflow

1. Pick a body (Earth / Moon / Mars). 2. Select a region with the point, rectangle or polygon tool — or load a preset ROI. 3. Press Run match: a Web Worker normalizes a 23-feature vector (8 analogy families) on fixed physical scales and ranks all 16 Earth analog sites with a weighted distance; each card shows what matches and where the analogy breaks. 4. Open Compare to inspect any pair side by side, with a shared cross-section chart.

The score, honestly

SI = 100 · (1 − d), where d = √( Σ w·Δ² / Σ w ) and Δ is the difference of each feature on its fixed physical scale. It is a similarity index, not a probability. Gravity, vacuum/pressure and radiation are shown as fixed gaps in Compare — no Earth site can match them, so they are never scored. Moon/Mars relief and all thermal/climate rasters are models driven by documented regional parameters — labeled as such in the stats chip — not sensor DEMs. Earth catalog values are literature-compiled regional estimates.

Offline & fallbacks

Everything except imagery tiles is inline. If Cesium or WebGL is unavailable the app renders an interactive 2-D schematic globe with the same selection tools. Force that mode with ?fallback=1 in the URL. Imagery: Earth → Esri World Imagery (Blue Marble single-tile fallback); Moon → LROC WAC global mosaic via NASA Trek/USGS; Mars → Viking MDIM21 color mosaic (MOLA-controlled). Each falls back to a procedural schematic texture when the network is down.

Provenance chips

documented catalog parameters compiled from the dataset literature · modeled physical/empirical model (relief, thermal, climate) · inferred interpolated between control points. The References button lists all 87 sources in APA 7.

Transparent scoring

Methodology

The similarity index

Each region is described by 22 numeric features + 1 landform class, grouped into the eight analogy dimensions the challenge names. The feature set is body-agnostic: there is no absolute elevation (Earth, Moon and Mars have different datums), and thermal inertia is a within-body percentile because its absolute scale differs by an order of magnitude between worlds.

FamilyFeatures
Topographyslope mean & σ · roughness · local relief (5 km) · crater/pit density
Surfacealbedo · thermal-inertia percentile · rock abundance
Thermal & lightmin temperature · diurnal swing · time below 0 °C · noon sun elevation (computed from latitude + obliquity)
Water & icearidity · near-surface ground ice
Mineralogyolivine · pyroxene · plagioclase · evaporite/sulfate · Fe-oxide · clay
Processes & biodust/aeolian activity · vegetation cover (biological overprint)
Subsurfacecaves · lava tubes · pits
Landformgenesis class with a documented affinity matrix
SI = 100 · ( 1 − √( Σ w·Δ² / Σ w ) )
  • Fixed scales. Each feature is normalized against a fixed physical range (e.g. slope 0–30°, min temperature −240…30 °C), never against the current catalog. A site's score therefore does not change when other sites are added — the same metric works for a global Earth grid.
  • Weight. w comes from the mission profile (Landing, Resource, Habitat, Science) or your custom sliders; each family weight is split evenly across its features.
  • Landform. Δ = 1 − affinity (e.g. mare plain ↔ flood basalt = 0.8).
  • Where it breaks. Every feature with |Δ| ≥ 0.35 is listed on the card as a break point, so each result answers: what is similar, how similar, and what differs.
  • Fixed gaps. Gravity, surface pressure, radiation dose and day length are reported in Compare but never scored.

Family breakdown bars

The eight mini-bars on each card are the unweighted RMS similarity within each family, independent of the mission profile. They show why a site ranks where it does, not just the headline number.

Where each feature will come from

Catalog values are literature estimates for now. The backend will extract each one from open data: NASADEM / Copernicus DEM, MODIS LST / albedo / NDVI, ASTER GED, MERRA-2, GPM and RADARSAT / Sentinel-1 for Earth; LOLA, Diviner, LEND and Mini-RF for the Moon; MOLA, TES / THEMIS, CRISM and SWIM for Mars. Hover a row in Compare for its fixed scale.

Each value in Compare carries a data-tier chip: M measured — read directly from an instrument product (DEM, surface temperature, albedo, crater/pit catalogs); D derived — computed from measured products with a documented formula (percentiles, aridity, sun angle, spectral unmixing); P proxy — a stand-in where no global map exists yet (band-ratio minerals on Earth, permafrost from mean surface temperature, cave potential from lithology).

Validation against the literature

Before the first run we froze a list of Earth sites that published papers name as analogs of each target (Jezero → Lake Salda; Cerberus Palus → McCartys flow and Icelandic flood lavas; Gale → Mauna Kea hematite ridge; Shackleton → Haughton crater; Marius Hills → San Francisco Volcanic Field). Ranked by pure similarity among the 16 catalog sites, the expected anchor lands in the top 5 for 5 of 5 targets under the Landing, Resource and Habitat profiles and 4 of 5 under Science (random chance ≈ 31%). Mare Imbrium and Tharsis have no cited anchor in the catalog yet and are left out rather than forced.

Confidence tiers

The badge on each card reflects how well-constrained the target region's parameters are:

  • High — a documented preset or catalog site: parameters compiled from the dataset literature.
  • Medium — a freehand selection: parameters inverse-distance interpolated between documented control points.
  • Low — fully synthetic input with no nearby documented control (defensive default).

What is modeled, honestly

Moon/Mars relief is a seeded fractal model honoring documented base elevation, relief and crater-density controls — never presented as a measured DEM. Thermal and climate rasters are physical/empirical models driven by regional parameters. Earth catalog values are literature-compiled regional estimates. Every card carries a Limitations disclosure stating where the analogy breaks, and the References modal lists all 87 sources in APA 7.
